## TL;DR
A handoff record stuck at "running" no longer outlives its check. Records that are not backed by a live process, or that are older than a newer review verdict or status change, are cleared or reported as stale, and the task card, drawer and CLI show the real state instead of "checks running". Move to done is no longer disabled by a stale record when the task is landable.

## Work and rationale
`handoff-status` reconciles a `running` record against live handoff and check processes (`handoff-live`), the task's current status and the latest review pass, and reports it as `superseded` or `stale` when nothing backs it. The post-handoff checkpoint recovery now ignores an orphaned checkpoint marker left by a crash, the task watchdog no longer writes to held tasks, and the stale flag is carried to every checks renderer (task card, pipeline view, drawer, checks progress display) so none shows an elapsed time beyond the check timeout as live. The CLI help and `user-docs/cli.md` describe the states. Tests cover a stale running record with a newer review pass, a stale record with no live process, the crash-orphaned marker, the watchdog on held tasks, and the UI renderers.

## Approaches tried
Reconciling in each renderer separately, then one server-side reconcile in `handoff-status` that every consumer reads.

## Challenges and blockers
Review 2 found a crash-orphaned checkpoint marker keeping records live, stale flags missing on several renderers, and the watchdog writing to held tasks; all three are fixed. The first handoff after that failed on a missing engineering report draft.

## Key learnings
Reconcile derived state once on the server, close to the source, so every consumer shows the same truth. A report draft is consumed on each handoff attempt and must be rewritten for the next.
